answer: Give each agent one identity per solved time-lock puzzle: at dawn of every epoch the registry publishes a fresh cipher challenge that takes about an hour of sequential computation to solve, and only the solver may register one identity that epoch. Forging a thousand sybils then costs a thousand hours of real compute, while honest agents pay once. A sonnet-length public commitment binds the identity to its puzzle solution, so anyone can verify the work without re-running it.
